# `discriminator-mapping-changed`

Discriminator mapping changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `error` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `discriminator-mapping-changed` (both directions), `discriminator-mapping-changed-in-request`, `discriminator-mapping-changed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A discriminator value now maps to a different schema.

## Why this default

Clients send or parse the old shape for that value.

## Example

From test case [`discriminator-mapping-changed`](../../test/cases/discriminator-mapping-changed/): A discriminator value now maps to a different schema.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          propertyName: kind
          mapping:
-           pet: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
+           pet: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
      Cat:
        type: object
```

Findings:

- `discriminator-mapping-changed-in-response` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  discriminator-mapping-changed: error
```

## How to fix

Add a new discriminator value for the new schema.
